candidates.label: Count
candidates.comment: A numerical quantity representing the number of discrete items or entities.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Tourist
candidates.comment: A person who is traveling or visiting a place for pleasure or interest.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalFacility: A place where medical care is provided. Also called Hospital, Clinic, Healthcare center. Examples: isolation unit.

chosen_type.label: MedicalClinic
chosen_type.justification: An 'isolation unit' is a type of medical facility providing healthcare, which fits the general description of schema.org:MedicalClinic.

candidates.label: CovidTestingFacility
candidates.comment: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.

candidates.label: MedicalClinic
candidates.comment: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.

candidates.label: ParkingFacility
candidates.comment: A ParkingFacility is a civic structure providing space for parking vehicles. Also called parking lot, parking garage, car park. Examples: a multi-story parking garage, a supermarket parking lot, a valet parking service. Distinct from Road, which is for vehicle travel.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: MedicalContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a particular medical therapy. Also called contraindication, medical warning, therapy restriction. Examples: "pregnancy" for certain medications, "allergy to penicillin", "severe kidney disease".

types.embedding_query_text: SocialEvent: An organized occasion for people to gather and interact. Also called Gathering, Assembly, Meeting. Examples: public gatherings.

chosen_type.label: SocialEvent
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type definition and the mention 'public gatherings' perfectly align with schema.org:SocialEvent, an event focused on social interaction.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: DanceEvent
candidates.comment: A DanceEvent is a social gathering or organized occasion primarily focused on dancing. Also called dance party, ball, disco, social dance. Examples: A salsa night, a wedding reception with dancing, a school prom, a folk dance festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or exists. Also called Period, Time span, Length of time. Examples: two to 21 days, weeks.

chosen_type.label: TemporalDuration
chosen_type.definition: A period of time expressed in natural language.
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:Duration is too specific to ISO 8601 format, and other candidates are too specific. TemporalDuration captures natural language expressions of time periods.

candidates.label: CalendarYear
candidates.comment: A specific calendar year.

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A specific point or period within a day, expressed either precisely or in natural language.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A specified period of time between two dates.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: A period of time corresponding to one of the twelve divisions of a year.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: Symptom: A physical or mental feature that is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly a characteristic one of a particular disease. Also called Sign, Indication, Manifestation. Examples: fever, headache, tiredness.

chosen_type.label: MedicalSymptom
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Symptom' and the mentions 'headache' and 'tiredness' are subjective complaints, fitting schema.org:MedicalSymptom. 'Fever' can also be a subjective symptom.

candidates.label: MedicalSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalSign
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is an objective physical manifestation of a medical condition, discoverable by diagnostic tests or physical examination. Also called objective symptom, clinical sign, diagnostic finding. Examples: "fever", "rash", "high blood pressure", "swelling". Distinct from MedicalSymptom, which is subjective and reported by the patient.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: DDxElement
candidates.comment: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentMinistry: A department of a government, usually headed by a minister. Also called Ministry, Government department. Examples: health ministry.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type definition and the mention 'health ministry' perfectly align with schema.org:GovernmentOrganization, an organization that is part of a governmental body.

candidates.label: GovernmentOfficial
candidates.comment: An individual holding a position of authority in a government.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentAgency: A permanent or semi-permanent organization in the machinery of government responsible for the oversight and administration of specific functions. Also called Public agency, Government body. Examples: US public health authorities.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type definition and the mention 'US public health authorities' perfectly align with schema.org:GovernmentOrganization, an organization that is part of a governmental body.

candidates.label: GovernmentOfficial
candidates.comment: An individual holding a position of authority in a government.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: EmploymentAgency
candidates.comment: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: RebelGroup: An organized group that resists the government or ruling power. Also called Insurgent group, Militant group. Examples: M23 rebel group.

chosen_type.label: RebelGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organized group that resists the government or ruling power, often through armed conflict.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate accurately describes a group that resists government power; RebelGroup is a specific type of Organization.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.
